en.html:
The rear approach wound downward in a spiral.

Not much width. Not much headroom either. The Commander and his horse, Muramasa and I disguised as priests—those were all the moving things. Yet our progress was remarkably noisy, footsteps echoing through the narrow passage.

Let several dozen people run about in here together, and the ears would suffer for it.

en.html:
My first sight of Rokuhara's ruler with my own eyes left me with that one word.

This man was strong.
In body. In mind. In every possible sense.

Even the breadth of his back spoke of how thickly that strength was laid on.

Goodness...
Righteousness...
Neither was visible.

His strength was arrogant. Probably sustained by desire of the simplest kind.

The urge to dominate, made flesh?

But that alone did not disqualify him from ruling Yamato. I was not so dreamy as to think: put a clean, upright, moral man on top, and the country will arrange itself nicely.

A king with ideals and insufficient power might throw it into greater disorder. East or west, history offered no shortage of examples.

Moriuji Ashikaga overflowed with power. The fate of all Yamato and all its people would probably not weigh heavily on that back.

However greedy a tyrant he was—if the Yamato gathered in his arms was protected as a result...

As a ruler, was he right or wrong?

ja.html:
六波羅総帥を初めて肉眼視しての感想は、ただその
一言に尽きた。

　この男は強いのだ。
　肉体的に。精神的に。<ruby>ありとあらゆる意味で<rt>・・・・・・・・・・</rt></ruby>。

　太い背が強さの厚みを物語っている。

　善性……
　あるいは義性といったものは、見受けられない。

　その強さは傲岸である。
　おそらく、ごくごく単純な<ruby>欲望<rt>・・</rt></ruby>に支えられているの
だろう。

　支配欲の権化か。

　しかし、それをもって彼に大和の統治者たるの資格
無しとは言えない。
　清く正しく道義に生きる者が上に立てば国は治まる
――と信じ込むほど俺も夢見がちではなかった。

　理想のみあって力足らぬ王は、むしろ国を乱す。
　東西の歴史を紐解けば、その種の前例は枚挙に暇が
ない。

　足利護氏は力に満ち溢れている。
　この背は大和全土全国民の命運も、重しとはしない
だろう。

　如何に彼が強欲極まる暴君であろうと――
　その両腕の抱え込む大和が、<ruby>結果的に<rt>・・・・</rt></ruby>守られるので
あれば。

　果たして彼は、統治者として是か、非か。

en.html:
Under Rokuhara, the people's burdens had certainly grown far heavier than before. Repression of opponents was far more open and severe.

But therefore Rokuhara's rule was bad rule? That was too simple.

The circumstances also had to be considered.

Six years ago, Rokuhara had committed an enormous betrayal. Sold the country, ended the war, and taken power over Yamato. But suppose it had not betrayed the country. Suppose it had fought the League on the home islands. Would the land not have become scorched earth?

The Rokuhara shogunate was a model of militarism. Individual rights received practically no consideration. But without that military system? Was there no chance of the continent's disorder spilling into Yamato?

These six years had hardly been an age of harmony elsewhere in the world. Rokuhara had managed to get through them in something like peace—at least without fighting another country. Could the previous government have done the same? I did not know.

A historian a hundred years from now might call Rokuhara's rule the best available method.

But therefore Rokuhara's rule was bad rule? That was too simple.

The circumstances also had to be considered.

Six years ago, Rokuhara had committed an enormous betrayal. Sold the country, ended the war, and taken power over Yamato. But suppose it had not betrayed the country. Suppose it had fought the League on the home islands. Would the land not have become scorched earth?

The Rokuhara shogunate was a model of militarism. Individual rights received practically no consideration. But without that military system? Was there no chance of the continent's disorder spilling into Yamato?

These six years had hardly been an age of harmony elsewhere in the world. Rokuhara had managed to get through them in something like peace—at least without fighting another country. Could the previous government have done the same? I did not know.

A historian a hundred years from now might call Rokuhara's rule the best available method.

ja.html:
六波羅体制下において、それ以前より、国民の負担
が大きく増しているのは確かな事実だ。
　反体制派に対する弾圧も、以前とは比較にならぬ程
露骨であり厳格である。

　が。
　よって六波羅の統治は悪政だ――と決め付けるのは
一概視が過ぎよう。

　情勢というものも併せて評価せねばならない。

　六年前、六波羅は途方もない裏切りを行い、国家を
売り、大戦に幕を引いた。そして大和の政権を得た。
　だがもし、六波羅が裏切らず、連盟軍と本土決戦を
繰り広げていたら？　国土は焦土と化さなかったか？

　六波羅幕府は手本のような軍国主義を敷いており、
国民一人一人の権利は全く軽視されている。
　だがこの軍国主義体制がなかったら？　大陸情勢の
混迷が大和にも波及する可能性はなかったろうか？

　世界的に見て調和の時代とは言い難いこの六年間を、
六波羅は曲がりなりにも平穏に――少なくとも他国と
交戦することだけはなく――乗り切っているのだ。
　過去の体制で同じことができたかはわからない。

　百年後の歴史家は、六波羅の統治を「最善の手法」
として評価するのかもしれなかった。

en.html: Many people in present-day Yamato, seeing Rokuhara's tyranny with their own eyes, would probably feel as I did. But someone in a later age, standing far enough away to judge without those feelings, could surely reach such an assessment too. Kill Moriuji Ashikaga now. End the Rokuhara system—◆no one could promise that this would not set Yamato on a straight road to ruin.

But someone in a later age, standing far enough away to judge without those feelings, could surely reach such an assessment too.

Kill Moriuji Ashikaga now.
End the Rokuhara system—◆no one could promise that this would not set Yamato on a straight road to ruin.
